result.title: Do Not Train Away Uncertainty: Early Uncertainty Anchored Calibration
result.summary: Deep neural networks, including large language models, have achieved remarkable performance across various tasks. However, they are prone to overconfidence during training or fine-tuning. In this work, we observe a consistent phenomenon across different models that the early model is better calibrated, while later training or fine-tuning yields marginal accuracy gains but substantially increases calibration errors. Our analysis suggests that the early model retains uncertainty awareness in both its predictions and features, which is gradually lost with continued training. To avoid training away this uncertainty awareness, we propose \textbf{EUA-Cal}, a novel method that exploits the \textbf{E}arly model as an \textbf{U}ncertainty \textbf{A}nchor for \textbf{Cal}ibration. EUA-Cal introduces early prediction regularization to preserve early predictive uncertainty and prototype structure regularization to exploit uncertainty reflected in the early feature space, jointly mitigating overconfidence. Extensive experiments on image classification and multiple-choice question answering across eight diverse models demonstrate that EUA-Cal outperforms state-of-the-art calibration methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文观察到模型在训练早期校准更好，继续训练或微调只带来边际精度提升却明显加重过度自信，并提出 EUA-Cal：以早期模型作为不确定性锚，结合早期预测正则与特征空间原型结构正则，保留预测与特征中的不确定性；在图像分类和多选题问答上对比现有校准方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 不直接研究视觉 latent 推理，但「早期模型保留不确定性、可作校准锚」的思路，可能为 LVR 中的停止决策与证据充分性判断提供置信度线索，其在多模态推理场景的适用性可供核查。
